# Built-In Data Types

**Example status — excerpt:** source and payload fragments illustrate shared
contracts; individual datatype references own their complete behavior.

Data types are the structural and typed nodes in a `relflow` schema. `Branch`
names a shared context for child fields, usually a repeated collection such as
transactions or sessions. Tensorfields are typed leaves that read values,
encode state and content, hide selected positions, and decode targets.

Use constructor names from the package root in Python. Serialized schemas use
the lower-case `type` value.

Every leaf follows the same high-level path while owning its type-specific
content contract:

```text
direct schema projection OR explicit JMESPath query
  -> canonical ragged field -> validate -> tensorize state/content
  -> embed visible input
  -> optionally decode selected targets
  -> write a public payload
```

## Choose A Data Type

| Source value | Recommended type | Use a different type when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Continuous scalar | [`Number`](../data-types/number.qmd) | Numeric value is an ID, code, or class label. |
| Boolean | [`Boolean`](../data-types/boolean.qmd) | The source has more than two valued labels; use `Category`. |
| One bounded label | [`Category`](../data-types/category.qmd) | The value is a massive or unstable identifier; keep it as metadata or use `Hash` for equality without a vocabulary. |
| Zero or more labels | [`Set`](../data-types/set.qmd) | Labels have attributes or order; use `Branch`. |
| Repeated objects | [`Branch`](../data-types/branch.qmd) | Repetition is only an upstream storage artifact; preprocess or flatten. |
| Timestamp/calendar value | [`DateParts`](../data-types/dateparts.qmd) | Elapsed time or recency matters; derive a `Number`. |
| Large or unbounded identifier | [`Hash`](../data-types/hash.qmd) | The ID is intentionally a small, stable, globally learned label; use `Category`. |
| Precomputed dense vector | [`Vector`](../data-types/vector.qmd) | `relflow` should compute embeddings from strings; use `Text`. |
| Free-form text | [`Text`](../data-types/text.qmd) | The string is a bounded label; use `Category` or `Set`. |

The same raw shape can have different meaning:

- `"12345"` is a `Number` only if numeric distance and magnitude matter.
- `"12345"` is a `Category` if it is a bounded code or label.
- `"12345"` is a `Hash` if equality matters but a learned vocabulary does
  not.
- `["red", "sale"]` is a `Set` if membership is unordered.
- `[{"name": "red"}, {"name": "sale"}]` is a `Branch` if each item has
  fields or position.

## Keep Python Value Types Stable

Identity-backed `Category`, `Cluster`, and `Hash` fields require one declared
Python compatibility family per field within a batch. `Set` applies the same
rule to its member labels across all valued sets. Their built-in declarations
place `str` and `bytes` in separate families. This prevents order-dependent
Awkward coercion from silently changing label identity; normalize source values
in a preprocessor. For `Set`, a scalar `str` or `bytes` is one label rather than
an iterable of characters or byte integers.

These rules are owned by each datatype plugin through `Plugin(types=...)`; the
ragged engine does not contain a list of built-in leaf names. Tuple entries are
separate compatibility families, so `types=(str, bytes)` accepts either type
but rejects a batch that mixes them. A union is one compatible family, so
`types=(int | float,)` permits numeric promotion within a field.

RelFlow recursively prepares atoms inside list, tuple, and NumPy-array leaf
values and converts NumPy scalars to their Python equivalents before matching
the declared families. `None` and a whole-leaf prediction `"<MASK>"` are core
routing states, not plugin atom types. Container shape and datatype meaning
remain the tensorfield's responsibility.

## Value State And Content {#value-state}

State says what happened to a position; content carries the datatype-specific
value. They are deliberately separate.

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `valued` | A source value exists. This does not guarantee that vocabulary-backed content is known. |
| `null` | The source value is explicitly `None`. |
| `padded` | A fixed branch shape contains a slot with no source item. |
| `masked` | The input at this position is intentionally hidden. |
| `other` | Reserved for extension-specific state. Current built-in tensorizers do not produce it from ordinary source data. |

There is no `pruned` state token. Pruning is an operation: a selected field is
hidden with input state `masked`, its original state and content are cached as
targets, and its trainable mask marks the positions that contribute to loss.
`target=True` is the always-pruned configuration.

Likewise, unavailable is not a universal state. It is a type-specific content
condition:

- an out-of-vocabulary `Category` remains `valued`, uses an internal sentinel,
  and contributes zero categorical content to the encoder;
- unknown `Set` members are omitted from its multi-hot content;
- types without a vocabulary do not need categorical availability semantics.

This distinction lets the model tell “a value was supplied but I do not know
its label” from `null`, padding, or an intentionally hidden input.

```json
[
  {"tags": ["vip"]},
  {"tags": []},
  {"tags": null},
  {}
]
```

For `Set("tags")`, `["vip"]` and `[]` are both valued. `null` is a null field
state. A missing repeated slot inside a `Branch` is padded. If a leaf has
`nullable=False`, encoding raises when its projected input contains an explicit
null.

Do not infer state from a numeric or categorical content sentinel. Neutral zero
content can represent several non-valued conditions, a real numeric zero, an
empty valued Set, or type-specific unavailable content. Tensorfield embedders
combine content with a separate state embedding before the value enters the
model.

## Shared Leaf Options

Every tensorfield inherits shared leaf options. Individual datatype pages own
their type-specific options. `Branch` has structural settings because it groups
children instead of reading one leaf value.

### Schema Identity

| Option | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `None`; inferred when bound | Public schema name and default processed-observation key. The normal `Model(..., amount=rf.Number)` or `Branch(..., amount=rf.Number)` keyword binding supplies `amount`; an unbound leaf must acquire a name before schema compilation. |
| `query` | `None` | Optional JMESPath source expression. `None` uses direct schema-address projection; no query is inferred. Explicit and direct values converge during eager coalescing before paired value/state regularization. See [Advanced Query Paths](querypaths.qmd). |
| `description` | `None` | Optional schema metadata. |
| `active` | `True` | Inactive fields remain in the schema but are ignored by encoding, loss, and prediction. |
| `nullable` | `True` | Allows explicit `None` input. `False` raises whenever the encoded leaf contains state `null`. |

### Learning Roles

| Option | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | `False` | Exact shorthand for `p_prune=1.0`; withholds the leaf from input and trains it as a supervised reconstruction target. |
| `p_mask` | `0.0` | Bernoulli rate for independently selecting leaf positions during non-predict masking. Must be less than `1.0`. |
| `p_prune` | `0.0` | Probability of selecting an observation and hiding the whole leaf instance for that observation. |
| `weight` | `1.0` | Positive multiplier applied to this field's total loss. |

The current `p_mask` implementation samples every configured position, including
null and padded positions, rather than valued positions only. `p_prune` samples
once per observation and expands that choice across all positions of the leaf.
Their cached original states allow state loss to learn what was hidden; each
datatype decides which selected targets contribute to content loss. See
[Dynamic Masking](dynamic-masking.qmd) for the exact behavior and branch masks.

`target=True` and `p_prune=1.0` are the supported always-hidden APIs.
`p_mask=1.0` is invalid because `p_mask` is constrained to rates below `1.0`.

### Decoder And Output Options

| Option | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `embed` | `False` | Requests a normalized embedding at this address during prediction. It does not make the field a target. See [Learning Modes & Embeddings](embeddings.qmd). |
| `pooling` | `"query"` | Target decoder pooling: `"query"` or `"mean"`. |
| `n_heads` | `4` | Even positive attention-head count. With `pooling="query"`, it must divide `d_model` and leave at least two dimensions per head; mean pooling constructs no query attention. |
| `dropout` | `None` | Optional query-pooling dropout rate below `1.0`. |
| `n_linear` | `1` | Positive number of learned-query cross-attention pooling blocks. Each block contains cross-attention and a feed-forward network. |

## Prediction Support

| Type | Public decoded content | State probabilities | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Number` | Scalar value | Yes | MAE and RMSE are reported in original value scale. |
| `Boolean` | Probability of `True` | Yes | Vocabulary-free binary decoding; configured thresholds affect metrics only. |
| `Category` | Best populated-vocabulary label plus optional candidates | Yes | The unavailable sentinel is internal and never a class. |
| `Set` | Per-label probabilities or thresholded labels | Yes | Unknown labels and unused capacity are omitted. |
| `Vector` | Reconstructed vector | Yes | Non-valued tensorized content is a zero vector. |
| `DateParts` | None | No public payload | Trains state accuracy plus per-part cosine loss and angular error. |
| `Hash` | None | No public payload | Reconstructs quantized hash lanes for training diagnostics. |
| `Text` | None | No public payload | Reconstructs frozen encoder embeddings, not text. |
| `Branch` | None | No | Child leaves may decode; `embed=True` can export branch context. |

No public decoded payload does not mean a field is ignored. `DateParts`,
`Hash`, and `Text` can be visible inputs, train reconstruction objectives, and
emit an embedding when configured with `embed=True`.

## Prediction Envelope

Decoded leaf writers share one address-keyed outer contract. The complete
structure and transport-specific shapes are documented in
[Prediction Output](../guides/prediction-output.qmd). In summary:

- `state` contains a probability for each token in the five-state vocabulary.
  Its arrays follow the schema shape for that leaf.
- `content` is owned by the datatype. It may be a number, Boolean payload,
  label/candidate payload, Set probability mapping, or vector.
- `inferred` is a Boolean mask, not a confidence score. During prediction it is
  true exactly where the encoded input state was `masked`.

An always-hidden `target=True` field and a predict-time `"<MASK>"` placeholder
therefore have `inferred=true` at their hidden positions. A visible leaf decoded
because it has `embed=True` may still produce state and content with
`inferred=false`. Consumers should use `inferred` to distinguish requested
inference from an auxiliary visible-field decode.

Root and branch embedding-only outputs do not have this decoded-leaf envelope.
They contain `embedding`; datatype pages explicitly say when their leaf writer
does not expose state or content. Rendered examples often use string paths for
readability, while the Python dictionary is keyed by `rf.Address` objects.

The public `embedding` is also distinct from tensorized content and the
datatype's internal input embedding. See
[Internal And Exported Embeddings](embeddings.qmd#internal-and-exported-embeddings).
